title: Runr — Jobs E2E: acquisition → enrichment → app

panels.title: Start here: what is happening in the last 30 minutes

options.content: **Read downward: eligible companies → collection → stored jobs → deletions → import → publication → enrichment → matching → app visibility.** Counts are live measurements, not targets. Stage inventories overlap; do not add them. Published membership is separate from the app query. A flat line plus stale telemetry is unknown, not success. Logs below retain actual batch timings. New telemetry history starts at installation; no history is invented.

panels.title: Published catalog / app query / function-indexed / current matching facts
Net published and app-query change in selected time range
panels.description: Net change includes removals. It is not gross newly published jobs. Requires at least two samples.

panels.title: Current blockers: failed workers, lock wait and enrichment review/source failures
panels.description: Service failure is the most recent systemd result and may be historical for a disabled unit. Lock wait is scoped to the one-time backfill process tree. Queue counts are current published versions.

options.content: Manifest counts are the reviewed input snapshot, not a count of jobs. Employer exclusions apply during collection and publication.

options.content: Latest completed collector-run gauges repeat between runs. These are outcomes per run, not counters to rate(). Requests and failed details explain low yield.

panels.description: Latest-run company scan outcomes and detail attempts within the last 2,000 durable attempt rows. The truncation indicator identifies partial detail coverage. Includes incomplete/running runs; no completed result is invented.

panels.title: Detail-attempt window truncated: 1 means partial coverage
Employer company scan state and coverage across time
panels.description: Cumulative current company checkpoints and coverage receipts, not latest-run newly collected jobs. A historical no_jobs state does not prove a fresh complete scan.

panels.title: Effective collector and normal publisher limits
panels.description: Explicit effective environment values only; absent settings are not replaced with guessed defaults. One-time backfill uses separate process overrides.

options.content: Durable producer inventory is not newly collected or publishable inventory. The age breakdown joins the retention index to existing rows; deleted index entries are excluded.

panels.title: Source jobs: stored / recent-date / expired-date / unknown-date

options.content: Thirty-day cleanup deletes source payloads and related search/detail rows. Retirement tombstones prevent resurrection. Recent-date counts still include jobs blocked by other policies.

panels.title: Latest physical cleanup batch and pass-completion evidence
5. Snapshot producer states and read the import window

options.content: The one-time backfill waits on shared publisher/source locks, takes consistent SQLite snapshots, then releases source locks. Bootstrap completion is explicit; rowid is not a count of jobs.

panels.title: Bootstrap complete and time since checkpoint advance
6. Normalize, resolve company ownership and deduplicate

options.content: Exact identities and source relationships determine merging. Batch execution timing below covers normalization and persistence; unsupported identities remain blocked, not fabricated.

panels.title: Delivery and large-company chunks per selected interval
Input job rows processed in the selected time range
panels.description: Rows in observed delivery events; retries may reprocess identities. This is not unique new published jobs. History begins when this counter was installed.

panels.title: 7. Save canonical jobs, observations and posting versions

options.content: Catalog lifecycle inventory is separate from publication. Unchanged source content reuses posting versions. Source history and user records can remain after a job disappears from discovery.
Age, employer exclusions, blue-collar decisions, application policy, ownership, duplicates and completeness determine eligibility. Rejection reasons can overlap; totals are not unique rejected jobs.

panels.title: 9. Commit the published catalog; expire ineligible membership

options.content: A successful commit advances the public head. Lifecycle expiry removes membership and marks canonical jobs expired while preserving identities, versions and customer history. This is not physical disk reclamation.

panels.title: Publication batches per sample interval
panels.description: Observed finished publication calls, including no-op/replay calls. Use membership/app net change to measure count movement, not this event count.

panels.title: Lifecycle expiry and physical deletion: latest receipt
10. Queue enrichment for current published versions

options.content: Counts are restricted to current versions in the current head. Historical/superseded queue entries are excluded. pending/running/review states are distinct.

panels.title: Current published-job enrichment queue across time
11. Classify white/blue collar and assign job functions

options.content: Current-version function memberships drive discovery. Blue jobs are excluded. A recent source posting without a usable function is not automatically discoverable.

panels.title: Current published jobs with indexed functions

options.content: Descriptions are supported by original-source quotations. This coverage counts matching current description records, not a guarantee every record passes current UI validation.

panels.title: 13. Repair invalid output and fill missing fields

options.content: Missing source text, invalid classification and unsupported descriptions remain explicit failures/review states. Daily provider budget can stop workers; it is a real resource ceiling.

panels.title: Current published jobs with matching facts
15. Return discoverable jobs to the app

options.content: This read-only probe uses the serving repository against the VPS database with an empty synthetic disposition and no user preferences. It is an unfiltered backend baseline, not a signed-in browser acceptance test or your personal filtered count.

panels.title: Published membership versus serving repository query
16. Reclaim historical storage and check VPS capacity

options.content: Hidden/expired jobs, deleted SQL rows and reclaimed filesystem bytes are different. SQLite free pages are reusable inside the file; they do not automatically shrink it. These panels measure actual database/WAL and filesystem bytes.

panels.title: Database files, allocated disk, WAL and reusable pages
Resource constraints: which stage is limited?

options.content: Per-service memory/CPU/task limits come from effective systemd properties; enrichment limits come from its installed command. CPU usage is measured between snapshots. Missing unlimited values remain absent. Host metrics come from Alloy node_exporter.

Execution evidence: batch timings and stage health

options.content: Sanitized logs contain stage names, counts, durations and error classes. No job text, account profiles or credentials are shipped. Use the time picker to inspect a stalled interval.
